problem: Linear attention variants lack general-purpose, hardware-efficient kernels and scalable distributed implementations compared to optimized softmax attention.
approach: A domain-specific compiler that decomposes linear attention into three canonical phases (intra-chunk computation, inter-chunk state propagation, output merging) and automatically generates fused, high-performance kernels from PyTorch code.
contribution: Forge enables 1.01x-4.9x performance improvements on diverse linear attention variants and scales to 16 million tokens on 128 GPUs with up to 7.2x speedup over prior distributed baselines.

problem: Traditional model merging suffers from task conflicts that degrade performance when consolidating multiple specialized models into a single unified model.
approach: Systematically compares RL-trained and SFT-trained LLMs, finding that RL reduces task conflicts through smaller-magnitude gradient updates, converging progressively, and joint optimization of positive/negative examples.
contribution: RL-trained LLMs significantly reduce task conflicts during model merging compared to SFT, with less performance degradation after merging across five representative tasks.

problem: fMRI signals are temporally irregular and noisy; existing self-supervised methods discard critical temporal information by discretizing or averaging.
approach: Reframes self-supervised learning as a Stochastic Optimal Control problem that models brain activity as continuous-time latent dynamics and learns a representation-agnostic control policy.
contribution: Demonstrates state-of-the-art performance on diverse downstream applications, unifying masked autoencoding and joint-embedding prediction while maintaining computational efficiency on large-scale fMRI datasets.

problem: Thinking LLMs overthink on simple problems while non-thinking LLMs underthink on hard reasoning, creating separate model variants and leaving end-users to select the optimal model.
approach: Introduces a unified benchmark with OverthinkingBench (72 domains of simple queries) and UnderthinkingBench (11 challenging reasoning tasks) using thinking-adjusted accuracy metrics to jointly evaluate both phenomena.
contribution: Shows that no model optimally thinks on the benchmark; thinking models often waste hundreds of tokens on simplest queries without improvement, highlighting the need for better unified models.

problem: Indirect 2D-to-3D editing methods for Gaussian Splatting introduce cross-view inconsistencies and constrain editing flexibility and efficiency.
approach: Proposes VF-Editor, which predicts attribute variations for Gaussian primitives directly in 3D using a novel variation predictor distilled from 2D editing knowledge and parallel decoding functions.
contribution: Enables flexible knowledge transfer from diverse 2D editors into a single unified 3D predictor, revealing limitations of indirect pipelines and validating native 3D editing effectiveness.

problem: Constraint-based causal discovery is hindered by prohibitive computational costs of conditional independence tests that scale poorly with sample size.
approach: Proposes E-CIT, a divide-and-aggregate framework that partitions data into subsets, applies base CITs independently to each, and aggregates p-values using a stable-distribution-grounded method.
contribution: Reduces computational complexity of base CITs to linear in sample size when subset size is fixed, achieving competitive performance while significantly reducing computational burden on causal discovery.

problem: Program induction faces a trade-off: symbolic methods generalize compositionally but don't scale; neural methods are flexible but fail to generalize systematically.
approach: Introduces Neural Language Interpreter (NLI), which learns its own discrete symbolic programming language end-to-end, discovers primitive operations, and uses a differentiable neural executor for gradient-based optimization.
contribution: Achieves better performance than in-context learning and test-time training on complex problems, enabling programs that represent arbitrary computation steps beyond training length through gradient-based test-time adaptation.

problem: Multimodal LLMs struggle to disentangle semantically similar actions in open-vocabulary scenarios due to reliance on text-centric priors and cross-modal hallucination.
approach: Decomposes actions into discriminative sub-motions and dynamically invokes domain-specific tools via reinforcement learning, creating category-specific reasoning without explicit supervision.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on HMDB-51, UCF-101, SSv2, Kinetics-400, and Kinetics-600, distinguishing fine-grained actions with computational efficiency while reducing cross-modal hallucination.

problem: Combining Chain-of-Thought with RL for text-to-image generation is effective but the underlying interaction between exploration and optimization is unclear.
approach: Provides entropy-based analysis showing CoT expands exploration space while RL contracts it; proposes EG-GRPO which reallocates optimization budget based on token uncertainty to preserve stability while encouraging structured exploration.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on standard T2I benchmarks by excluding low-entropy tokens from reward updates and adding entropy bonuses to high-entropy tokens.

problem: Process-Supervised RL for reasoning models suffers from limited exploration efficiency in both branching positions and sampling strategies.
approach: Proposes AttnRL which branches from positions with high attention scores, develops adaptive sampling based on problem difficulty and historical batch size, and designs one-step off-policy training.
contribution: Consistently outperforms prior PSRL approaches on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks in terms of performance and sampling/training efficiency.

problem: Transformers fail to capture intrinsic temporal structure and are susceptible to real-world noise and anomalies in time series forecasting.
approach: Proposes Local Geometry Attention (LGA) grounded in local Gaussian process theory that learns query-specific distance metrics and introduces TSRBench, a robustness benchmark with realistic corruptions.
contribution: LGA significantly reduces performance degradation under noise, consistently outperforming Transformer and linear models on TSRBench and establishing a foundation for robust real-world time series deployment.

problem: KV cache technology for sequential recommendation reduces latency but introduces substantial storage overhead for long user history sequences across large user bases.
approach: Proposes CollectiveKV which observes that KV sequences across users exhibit significant similarities; uses SVD to decompose into shared and user-specific components, storing shared KV in a learnable global pool.
contribution: Compresses KV cache to 0.8% of original size while maintaining or enhancing model performance across five recommendation models and three datasets.

problem: Grounding formal logic in natural language remains fragmented, with datasets that are small-scale, domain-specific, or translate logic into overly technical forms rather than context-rich language.
approach: Introduces VERIFY, a large-scale dataset with 200k+ rigorously generated triplets of LTL formulas, Intermediate Technical Language (ITL) bridge representations, and domain-specific NL descriptions across 13 domains.
contribution: Provides high-fidelity data with model-checking-verified LTL formulas, estimated >97% semantic correctness via Llama 3.3, and demonstrates scalability and logical complexity for bridging formal methods and NLP.

problem: Linear attention variants lack general-purpose, hardware-efficient kernels and scalable distributed implementations compared to optimized softmax attention.
approach: A domain-specific compiler that decomposes linear attention into three canonical phases (intra-chunk computation, inter-chunk state propagation, output merging) and automatically generates fused, high-performance kernels from PyTorch code.
contribution: Forge enables 1.01x-4.9x performance improvements on diverse linear attention variants and scales to 16 million tokens on 128 GPUs with up to 7.2x speedup over prior distributed baselines.

problem: Group-robust generalization in the presence of spurious correlations is difficult without bias annotations, and existing CCDB methods oversimplify distributions as single Gaussians.
approach: Proposes MST (Multi-stage data-Selective reTraining) which uses hard confusion matrix to describe distributions finely, enabling FG-CCDB with confusion-cell-wise reweighting from a global perspective.
contribution: Achieves performance on par with bias-supervised approaches on binary classification and significantly outperforms them on highly biased multi-class and multi-shortcut scenarios without bias labels.

problem: Low sample efficiency of on-policy RL algorithms limits safe adaptation of humanoid control policies to new environments despite successful large-scale pretraining.
approach: Uses off-policy SAC with large batch updates for large-scale pretraining, then finetunes using model-based methods where deterministic policies execute in the environment while stochastic exploration is confined to a physics-informed world model.
contribution: Couples wall-clock efficiency of large-scale simulation during pretraining with sample efficiency of model-based learning during finetuning, enabling zero-shot deployment and efficient adaptation on humanoids.

problem: Regression losses like MSE assume unimodal Gaussian distributions and fail to capture complex patterns where multiple diverse outcomes are possible in time series forecasting.
approach: Proposes Multi-Mode Patch Diffusion (MMPD) loss that models future distribution using a diffusion model conditioned on latent tokens, with multi-mode inference fitting an evolving Gaussian Mixture Model during diffusion.
contribution: Generates diverse predictions with corresponding probabilities on eight datasets, matching or exceeding deterministic/probabilistic capabilities of MSE and Student-T losses.

problem: GPTQ is a standard LLM quantization method but its algebraic updates obscure geometric meaning and lack worst-case performance guarantees.
approach: Proves GPTQ executed back-to-front is mathematically identical to Babai's nearest plane algorithm for the closest vector problem on a lattice defined by Hessian matrices, inheriting Babai's error bounds.
contribution: Provides geometric interpretation of GPTQ error propagation and designs post-training quantization methods avoiding clipping that outperform original GPTQ while providing efficient GPU inference kernels.

problem: Pure exploration requires agents to efficiently collect data to identify underlying correct hypotheses, but adaptive hypothesis testing remains computationally challenging.
approach: Proposes In-Context Pure Exploration (ICPE) which meta-trains Transformers to map observation histories to query actions and predicted hypotheses, enabling in-context transfer without parameter updates.
contribution: Across deterministic, stochastic, and structured benchmarks including BAI and generalized search, ICPE is competitive with adaptive baselines while requiring no explicit modeling of information structure.

problem: Fine-tuning diffusion models for reward-guided generation in biomolecular design struggles with instability, low sample efficiency, and mode collapse when using on-policy RL methods.
approach: Proposes an iterative distillation-based framework that casts finetuning as policy distillation: collects off-policy data, simulates soft-optimal policies, and minimizes KL divergence between policies.
contribution: Enhances training stability and sample efficiency compared to RL-based methods while achieving effective reward optimization across protein, small molecule, and regulatory DNA design tasks.

problem: Discovering neural mechanisms underlying cognitive behavior requires iterative refinement of network architectures and objectives, creating a long human-in-the-loop design process.
approach: Trains RNNs to reproduce human cognitive errors using non-parametric generative models for surrogate data and novel diffusion model-based training that captures all statistical moments in behavioral response distributions.
contribution: Network dynamics correctly predict previously reported qualitative features of neural data from macaques on visual working memory tasks, including characteristic swap errors.

problem: Vision-Language Models suffer from learned spurious correlations that compromise performance, but existing mitigation strategies require auxiliary data, retraining, labeled features, or external models.
approach: Proposes DIAL, a zero-shot interpretable method using distributional analysis to filter representations, sparse autoencoders to disentangle and identify spurious feature directions, then removes those subspaces.
contribution: Consistently outperforms or matches existing baselines on spurious correlation benchmarks in terms of overall and worst-group accuracy without requiring auxiliary data or external supervision.

problem: Visual prompt tuning lacks interpretability, which is essential for enhancing AI reliability and enabling knowledge discovery, while current approaches learn abstract prompt embeddings.
approach: Proposes IVPT which links visual prompts to human-understandable semantic concepts via cross-layer concept prototypes, aggregating region features to generate interpretable prompts for multiple network layers.
contribution: Achieves superior interpretability and performance over visual prompt tuning and existing interpretable methods on fine-grained classification benchmarks with different network depth explanations.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting lacks explicit encoding of structural sparsity in covariances and uncertainty estimates, leaving noise-dominated components insufficiently regularized.
approach: Introduces a Bayesian extension placing global-local Horseshoe priors on covariance scales, using factorized variational inference with Monte Carlo rendering to enable pixel-wise posterior uncertainty.
contribution: Produces high-quality uncertainty maps while matching state-of-the-art 3DGS visual fidelity and runtime, with theoretical posterior contraction guarantees and robustness to structured covariance sparsity.

problem: Existing SNNs based on first-order ODEs with Markovian dynamics fail to capture long-range correlations and fractal dendritic structures observed in real neurons.
approach: Proposes fractional-order SNNs (f-SNNs) generalizing integer-order SNNs using fractional-order ODEs to model brain activity with long-term dependencies and non-Markovian behavior.
contribution: Fractional adaptations achieve superior accuracy, comparable energy efficiency, and improved robustness to noise compared to integer-order SNNs, with released open-source toolbox supporting diverse architectures.

problem: Retrieval Augmented Generation systems in dynamic domains like gaming lack dedicated benchmarks due to Dual Dynamics (game content updates and shifting player community focus) and authenticity requirements.
approach: Proposes ChronoPlay, a framework with dual-dynamic update mechanisms to track both content and community changes, and dual-source synthesis from official sources and player communities for authentic query patterns.
contribution: Creates the first dynamic RAG benchmark for gaming, providing new insights into model performance under complex and realistic conditions with instantiation on three distinct games.

problem: Zeroth-order optimizers avoid memory bottlenecks of first-order optimizers like Adam but require tens of times more convergence steps, creating a fundamental speed-memory trade-off.
approach: Introduces FZOO, which reduces convergence steps via batched one-sided estimates with adaptive step-sizes based on loss standard deviation, and accelerates per-batch computation using Rademacher random perturbations.
contribution: On average outperforms MeZO by +3% accuracy while requiring 3x fewer forward passes; for RoBERTa-large achieves +5.6% improvement and 18x reduction in forward passes, reaching Adam-scale convergence speed.

problem: Existing hyperbolic neural networks mix Euclidean and hyperbolic operations or rely on extrinsic parameterizations, failing to be fully intrinsic to the hyperbolic geometry.
approach: Proposes ILNN, a fully intrinsic architecture conducting computations within the Lorentz model, with novel point-to-hyperplane fully connected layer using hyperbolic distances and intrinsic modules (GyroLBN, gyro-additive bias, patch-concatenation).
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance and computational cost among hyperbolic models while consistently surpassing Euclidean baselines on CIFAR-10/100 and genomic benchmarks.

problem: Active learning label complexity for decision trees as binary classifiers lacks theoretical understanding and analysis under non-restrictive assumptions.
approach: Provides first analysis of the disagreement coefficient for decision trees under grid-like input structure and distinct feature queries per path, presents first general active learning algorithm with multiplicative error guarantees.
contribution: Achieves polylogarithmic label complexity in dataset size under stated assumptions, with label complexity lower bound showing algorithm dependence on error tolerance epsilon is close to optimal.

problem: Diverse 3D understanding tasks (depth estimation, novel view synthesis, object manipulation) are addressed in isolation, preventing shared representations and cross-task knowledge transfer.
approach: Presents 3WM, a probabilistic graphical model with multimodal scene elements, where different inference pathways through the graph yield different tasks without task-specific training.
contribution: Outperforms specialized baselines without finetuning while providing precise controllability, strong geometric consistency, and robustness; achieves state-of-the-art on NVS and 3D object manipulation with composable inference pathways.

problem: First-order optimizers like Adam increase memory usage to over 10 times inference level during full-parameter LLM fine-tuning, creating a critical GPU memory bottleneck.
approach: Proposes ABSignSGD, a block-coordinate variant of sign-based descent with flexible block selection, featuring majority-vote extension for distributed training using only gradient sign aggregation.
contribution: On Qwen3-8B, Llama3-8B, and Qwen3-32B converges faster per iteration with superior downstream performance while reducing runtime and memory compared to existing methods.

problem: LLM pretraining requires both high data quantity and quality, but existing datasets struggle to balance these requirements effectively.
approach: Introduces GneissWeb, a 10 trillion token dataset using sharded exact sub-string deduplication and an ensemble of quality filters including novel components for favorable quality-quantity trade-off.
contribution: Models trained on GneissWeb outperform those trained on FineWeb-V1.1.0 by 2.73 percentage points on average across 11 benchmarks and 1.75 points on 20 benchmarks.

problem: Direct application of RL to multimodal reasoning struggles to activate complex reasoning, and current training pipelines do not effectively balance perceptual grounding with cognitive reasoning.
approach: Introduces staged training: text-only cold start for initialization, multimodal GRPO addressing gradient stagnation, then text-only RL to enhance multimodal reasoning capabilities.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art among open-source 7B MLLMs on challenging benchmarks including MathVerse, MathVision, WeMath, LogicVista, DynaMath, and AIME2024/2025.

problem: LLM-based recommendation faces challenges: LLMs struggle with long noisy user histories that exceed token limits, and CoT requires expensive autoregressive rationale generation at inference.
approach: Proposes SIREN which builds compact interest sketches from user histories via semantic topic clustering, then learns to internalize chain-of-thought reasoning into model parameters through hidden alignment.
contribution: Enables effective LLM-based rating prediction with near-CoT quality at inference while drastically reducing latency through internalized reasoning without explicit rationale generation.

problem: Automated knowledge graph construction from scientific literature struggles with long multi-word entity recognition, lacks domain generalization, and overlooks hierarchical/logically constrained scientific knowledge.
approach: Proposes two-stage framework: Z-NERD uses Orthogonal Semantic Decomposition and Multi-Scale TCQK attention for entity recognition; HGNet uses hierarchy-aware message passing with Differentiable Hierarchy Loss and Continuum Abstraction Field Loss.
contribution: Enables scalable, zero-shot scientific KG construction that recognizes long entities, generalizes across domains, and explicitly models hierarchical structure and abstraction levels in knowledge graphs.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting requires copyright protection and efficient compression, but compression techniques like quantization degrade the integrity of existing watermarking methods.
approach: Proposes compression-tolerant 3DGS watermarking that embeds watermarks into anchor attributes, uses quantization distortion layer to preserve watermarks after compression, and employs frequency-aware anchor growing strategy.
contribution: Preserves watermark integrity and rendering quality under compression while maintaining high visual fidelity through HSV loss to mitigate color artifacts.

problem: Large neural network architectures for time-series anomaly detection incur high computational costs and memory usage, making them impractical for real-time and resource-constrained scenarios.
approach: Proposes PaAno, a lightweight method extracting short temporal patches and using 1D CNN embeddings with triplet loss and pretext loss to capture informative temporal patterns.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on TSB-AD benchmark for univariate and multivariate anomaly detection, significantly outperforming methods based on heavy architectures.

problem: Matrix completion via deep linear networks shows implicit low-rank bias in deeper networks, but prior theory focuses on shallow models and lacks explanation of this depth-dependent phenomenon.
approach: Analyzes matrix completion via deep matrix factorization showing coupled dynamics intensifies with depth, proving convergence to rank-1 occurs if and only if dynamics are coupled.
contribution: Explains loss of plasticity phenomenon in matrix completion, showing deep models avoid plasticity loss through low-rank bias while depth-2 networks fail, providing mechanistic insight into depth effects.

problem: Fairness metrics conflict philosophically and their conflicting assumptions hinder unified paradigms in UMLLMs where biases propagate systemically across understanding and generation.
approach: Introduces IRIS Benchmark which synchronously evaluates fairness of understanding and generation in UMLLMs using demographic classifier ARES and four datasets with 60 metrics across three fairness dimensions.
contribution: Uncovers systemic phenomena like generation gap, personality splits, and counter-stereotype reward while offering diagnostics to guide UMLMM fairness optimization, resolving fairness metric conflicts.

problem: Learning physical dynamics from real-world observational data is challenged by incompleteness and irregular sampling, limiting applicability of existing data-driven approaches.
approach: Proposes a diffusion-based framework that strategically partitions samples into observed context and unobserved query components, training a conditional diffusion model to reconstruct missing portions.
contribution: Achieves asymptotic convergence to true complete generative process under mild conditions and significantly outperforms baselines on synthetic and real-world physics benchmarks including fluid flows and weather.
